scenes.say: Ever wondered how Go keeps your code organized and your dependencies in check? Let's break down packages and modules.

scenes.label: Package
scenes.sub: A package groups related Go files.
scenes.say: A package is simply a collection of related Go files. It's how you structure and reuse code.

scenes.label: Module
scenes.sub: A module manages dependencies and versions.
scenes.say: A module, introduced in Go one point eleven, manages your project's dependencies and versioning.

scenes.title: Module Setup
scenes.say: To start, run 'go mod init' to create a module. Use 'go get' to add dependencies. The go dot mod file keeps track of everything.

scenes.question: What does go.mod do?
scenes.right: It declares your module path and lists dependencies for reproducible builds.
scenes.say: Don't forget—go dot mod isn't just a project name. It declares your module path and lists dependencies for reproducible builds.
